description.narrative:
Overall goal Scaling up gender transformative approached in advocacy, accountability culture and partnership effectiveness to advance MEA regional impact and sustainability. The Strategic Plan 20142027 has three strategic areas and in total seven objectives:
Strategic area 1: Advocacy
Objective 1: Position MEA as a leading male engagement movement in the region within its thematic areas by mobilising collective voices and actions to influence policies and legal reforms.
Objective 2: Scale up gender transformative advocacy through capacity strengthening MEA's network and strategic partners to advance feminist approaches and principles.
Strategic area 2: Accountability
Objective 3: Improve systems and structures to operationalize and popularise existing MEA accountability mechanism for effective collaboration responsiveness and functionality of the movement.
Objective 4: Advance MEA's joint actions an initiatives through capacity strengthening of partners utilising country and regional channels to achieve MEA's goals
Strategic area 3: Partnerships
Objective 5: Implement capacity strengthening initiatives on gender transformative approached including MenEngage Africa Training Initiative (MATI)
Objective 6: Identify strengthen and maintain strategic partnerships for collaboration across MEA thematic areas at national, regional and global levels.
Objective 7: Contribute to resource mobilization for the sustainability of the MEA network

Men Engage Africa är ett av globala Men Engage Alliansens regionala nätverk. Men Engage Africa nätverket består av 22 nationella Men Engage Africa nätverk (Botswana, Burundi, Kamerun, Etiopien, Demokratiska Republiken Kongo, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Eswatini) med medlemmar på nationell nivå. Men Engage nätverket fokuserar hur maskulinitetsnormer är formade, hur de påverkar samhället, relationer och individer. Kärnan i nätverkets arbete är att bidra till jämställdhet mellan könen, förbättra sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR), och minska förekomsten av könsbaserat våld genom att engagera pojkar och män genom "gender transformation" - metoder som utmanar och förändrar negativa manlighetsnormer. Nätverket har etablerat sig som en ledande aktör på global, regional och nationell nivå inom detta fält sedan 2009.

The contribution is a project support to Sonke Gender Justice for the implementation of Men Engage Africa's Strategic Plan 2019-2024. The core of Men Engage Africa's work is qualitative work on men and masculinity within women’s rights, SRHR and gender justice for all with the aim to contributing to Gender Equality.

description.narrative:
Examples of results achieved:
The results summary covers the implementation period May 2019 to December 2023. The results are therefore structured according to and responds to the strategic objectives as they were structured and formulated in the Men Engage Africas previous Strategic plan 20192023. The overall objective of the plan was that by 2023, MEA and partners have more influence and impact across the region, and have contributed to increased support, uptake and implementation of feminist, gender transformative approaches to engaging men and boys for gender equality. (Strategic Objective 1) MEA has established itself as a highimpact network by strengthening its members' organisational capacities and creating a connected, cohesive structure across the continent. MEA's membership base increased from 22 countries in 2019 to 24 country coalitions and from 350 to over 500 organisations in 2023. The capacity building has included comprehensive capacity assessments for MEA partners, revealing substantial gaps in understanding and implementing the Gender Transformative Approach (GTA). To address the gaps MEA secretariat carried out in person trainings and linked partners to global dialogues on various topics to facilitate knowledge exchange. The secretariat further conducted strength assessments across MEA country networks to evaluate each networks and member organisations capacitity. The MEA secretariat further provided technical support on GTA implementation to various strategic partners, including Rutgers, Plan Finland, IAMANEH Sweis, Concern Worldwide, and UN Women. The various trainings led to MEA developing a checklist for integrating the transformation of masculinities into project activities. MEA has further strengthened its youth chapter and promoted youth leadership within the network. Initiatives like the 'Power to Youth' and Generation Gender have empowered young people to participate actively in gender justice advocacy and program implementation. From 2019 to 2023 MEA youth has developed a number of resources and tools, including the Media toolkit, a practical toolkit for young people who are passionate about creating change on matters impacting youth, such as eradicating harmful practices like Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting (FGM/C) and child marriage, sexual and genderbased violence (SGBV) and unintended pregnancies to be able to engage with different media platforms and use them as practical tools for advocacy. A Meaningful Youth Participation (MYIP) Checklist was developed in collaboration with CHOICE for Youth to serve as a guiding document when engaging with young people and when youthled organisations engage with adultled organisations. The checklist is meant to help organisations (youthled, youthserving or have young staff/volunteers) interrogate how they engage with young people and youth organisations to see them more than simply beneficiaries but as partners, stakeholders, and leaders. (Strategic objective 2) In terms of meeting the objective related to increased evidencebased implementation, MEA have continued to work with faith and traditional leader, especially through the MenCare campaign. Over the past four years, MenEngage Africa (MEA) has prioritised grassroots mobilisation by working closely with community leaders, faithbased organisations, and traditional authorities to promote gender equality. By engaging these key stakeholders, MEA has fostered community ownership of gendertransformative initiatives, ensuring that interventions are culturally relevant and sustainable. In Malawi and Namibia, MEA network partners have been working closely with these religious and traditional leaderssome network partners themselvesto challenge harmful traditional and religious norms related to fatherhood. Tools like the *Engaging Men in the Elimination of Child Marriage* manual have empowered religious and traditional leaders in countries like Nigeria and Kenya to commit to ending harmful practices such as unsafe abortion and Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) within their communities. MEA partners have further actively been engaging men as caregivers and fathers through advocacy initiatives at both local and national levels in 20 countries. The work has led to an increase in number of countries conducting research on fatherhood in Africa. Together with key partners, including Equimundo, Save the Children, Rutgers, and MEA Global, MenEngage Africa has developed a series of State of the World Fathers reports and country reports (South Africa and soon to be launched in Zimbabwe) with specific recommendations for shifting norms towards promoting positive parenting, parental leave policies, recognition, and redistribution of care work. The firstever African report on fatherhood, the State of South Africa Fathers Report, was published in 2018. The report sparked significant interest in other countries, leading to Uganda and Tanzania publishing their firstever State of Fathers Reports in 2021. South Africa followed up with a second edition of their report in 2021, with plans for a third edition in 2026. Rwanda and Zimbabwe joined the research initiative in 2023, with their fatherhood reports expected to be published in 2024. In terms of engaging men and boys in SRHR an important component has been focused on regional commitment development, where Sonke and MenEngage Africa played an instrumental role in a Technical Working Group that led to the creation of a West and Central Africa commitment. The commitment, endorsed by 24 ministers, focuses on ensuring that adolescents and young people are educated, healthy, and thriving, which is marking a political shift towards prioritizing youth SRHR issues. There has however been a lot of challenges connected to the work focused on SRHR. Country networks have reported difficulties securing sufficient funding and resources due to regressive laws on key SRHR issues such as safe abortion, CSE, and LGBTI rights. MEA partners have further utilised various forms of media, including print, social, and broadcast media, to amplify their message and drive their initiatives forward. In order to enhance outreach and engagement, the MEA secretariat strategically employs social media platforms, highlighting the work of its partners on both international and regional stages. MenEngage Africa, also organised several international and regional conferences in 2023, addressing genderbased violence, access to sexual reproductive rights, and other critical issues. Numerous press releases and opinion pieces have been published in response to rising human rights issues, such as Uganda's antihomosexuality bill and other matters concerning child rights, SRHR and GBV, and several articles were written over the four years highlighting these issues. (Strategic objective 3) MEAs work focused on contributing to a more enabling policy environment that promotes gender transformative approaches has involved active engagement in local, national, and international advocacy to promote the inclusion of men and boys in gender equality policies and programs. By participating in policy dialogues, submitting policy recommendations, and engaging with decisionmakers, MEA has contributed to integrate gendertransformative approaches into key policy frameworks at different levels, such as for example South Africa's National Strategic Plan on Genderbased violence and femicide 20202030, the Kenya AIDS Strategic Framework (KASF II) (2020/2021 2024/2025) and Ugandas National Plan of Action for Sexual and Gender Based Violence and Violence Against Children. Similar advocacy has taken place in Botswana and Nigeria, with MEA influencing language in the National Gender and Development policy as evidenced in the Universal Peer Review report submitted by Botswana in December 2020 and in the revised National HIV and AIDS Strategic Framework of Nigeria 20192021. A few other examples of what the MEA members advocacy work has led to is that Zimbabwe's Constitutional Court in 2022, effectively outlawed child marriages by raising the legal age of consent from 16 to 18. In 2023, Zambia followed suit by amending its 1918 Marriage Act to raise the minimum marriage age to 18 for all marriages, including those under customary law. In Malawi, MEA members successfully advocated for the launch of an Ending Child Marriage Strategy, leading to the 2023 Penal Code Amendment, which raised the age of consent from 16 to 18. MEA has further started to build strategic partnerships with regional economic communities, including the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the East African Community (EAC), and the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA). MEA have reengaged policymakers on critical issues such as the AntiCrossBorder FGM and EAC SRHR Bill. Together with the Eastern African SubRegional Support Initiative (EASSI), MEA has conducted sensitisation sessions with policymakers to enhance the implementation of existing laws and policies, aiming to close the gaps in addressing FGM and other harmful practices. In collaboration with SADC, MEAs efforts have centered on GBV prevention and implementing the SADC Model Laws on GBV and Child Marriages. MEA have also engaged private sector actors alongside CSOs and policymakers to encourage states to commit to ILO Convention 190 on Violence and Harassment. Over four years, six MEA countries have signed and ratified ILO Convention C190: Namibia (2020), South Africa (2021), Nigeria (2022), Uganda (2023), Lesotho (2023), and Rwanda (2024). (Strategic objective 4) MEA further continued its work on strengthening accountability to the sector, meaning that MEA and its country networks shall be held accountable to the SRHR, womens rights and gender justice movements, through policies and practices that are based on solidarity, equality, justice and feminist principles. Through a cocreation process coordinated by the Men Engage Global Alliance Secretariat and in collaboration with womens rights and gender justice partners to align with broader feminist principles, MEA participated in developing the MenEngage Accountability framework in 2023. The purpose of the framework is to ensure that MEA's actions directly respond to the priorities and needs identified by these movements, maintaining a focus on gender equality and social justice. MEA secretariat hosts regular dialogues and capacitybuilding sessions on Accountability Standards and Guidelines for its members. The sessions provide reflection, learning, and improvement opportunities, helping network members enhance their understanding of accountability and to effectively apply the principles in their work. As a result of popularising the accountability framework among members, the secretariat and the regional steering committee have received an increasing amount of reports of sexual harassment and fraud and have investigated several cases from country networks and successfully implemented the recommendations in the investigation reports.
